properties.description: Driven through the two steps call_tool takes around every handler (effective_writes_for, writes_for_precheck, serving_for): a declared session's writes are credited as author; a request's _meta name wins for that request only; nothing declared credits nothing; the declaration never adds an approver role; a name the design does not hold is refused before anything is written and a refused declaration does not stick; a declaration belongs to one session (share() starts with nobody); declaring nobody stops the crediting; the sessionless transport refuses a declaration. Plus the real binary driven over stdio on 2026-09-25 with a tools/call carrying _meta: credited to the _meta name, then to the declared session, and an unknown _meta name refused with the node not created.
properties.findings: 8 of 8 pass on branch feat/a-session-names-who-it-writes-for. With the crediting disabled on the write guard's release, the two crediting tests fail, so the check can fail.
properties.name: A session's or a request's named contributor is credited with every write, and never approves
